_comment: Daily, and deliberately not more often. This account is on Hobby,
which caps crons at one run per day, and Vercel does not clamp a
faster schedule or warn about it — it refuses to create the
deployment at all, with cron_jobs_limits_reached. A '* * * * *' here
silently blocked every push for hours: the deployment list showed
nothing failing because nothing was ever built.
The keeper's real cadence comes from cron-job.org at one minute,
which is what the 7200s randomness timeout actually needs. This entry
is only a backstop for the case where that external job dies, so a
round eventually gets closed and settled rather than sitting open
forever — an Open round cannot even time out and refund on its own.
If this project moves to Pro, a faster schedule becomes available and
this can carry the keeper by itself.
